protocol_meta.target_scope: minimal MQTT 3.1.1 broker subset for planning-agent debugging

channels.name: main
channels.purpose: Carries MQTT control packets between external clients and the broker over one ordered byte stream per accepted connection.

runtime_implications.summary: The broker runtime should accept TCP clients and use an event loop capable of read, write, and close dispatch.
Packet decoding must tolerate stream fragmentation and coalescing by keeping unread bytes in a per-connection input buffer.
Outbound MQTT packets are queued per connection and flushed through nonblocking socket writes.

roles.name: client
roles.summary: External MQTT clients initiate TCP connections, send CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, PINGREQ, and DISCONNECT packets, and receive broker responses or forwarded PUBLISH packets.

roles.name: broker
roles.summary: The generated target is a broker/server that accepts client connections, tracks sessions, records subscriptions, routes QoS0 publications, and emits acknowledgements or ping responses.

interaction_units.name: control_packet
interaction_units.summary: Each protocol unit is decoded from an MQTT fixed header, variable-length Remaining Length field, and packet-specific body.

interaction_units.name: application_message_delivery
interaction_units.summary: A QoS0 PUBLISH payload is routed to connected sessions whose topic filters match the publish topic.

core_flows.name: connection_establishment
core_flows.summary: Client sends CONNECT; broker records session information and replies with CONNACK accepted.

core_flows.name: subscription_management
core_flows.summary: Connected client sends SUBSCRIBE with one or more topic filters; broker stores filters and returns SUBACK with Granted QoS0 codes.

core_flows.name: publish_qos0_delivery
core_flows.summary: Connected client sends QoS0 PUBLISH; broker matches topic filters and forwards a QoS0 PUBLISH to each matching session.

core_flows.name: keepalive_probe
core_flows.summary: Connected client sends PINGREQ; broker replies with PINGRESP.

core_flows.name: client_disconnect
core_flows.summary: Client sends DISCONNECT; broker closes the connection and removes session subscriptions during close handling.

surface_catalog.name: CONNECT
surface_catalog.summary: Opens a broker session using MQTT protocol name, protocol level 4, connect flags, keepalive, and client identifier.

surface_catalog.name: CONNACK
surface_catalog.summary: Acknowledges CONNECT with a session-present flag and return code; the example broker sends accepted.

surface_catalog.name: SUBSCRIBE
surface_catalog.summary: Registers one or more topic filters with requested QoS values; fixed header low flags must be 0x02.

surface_catalog.name: SUBACK
surface_catalog.summary: Acknowledges a SUBSCRIBE packet with the original packet identifier and one return code per topic filter.

surface_catalog.name: PUBLISH
surface_catalog.summary: Carries a topic name and application payload; this example broker routes only QoS0 messages and forwards QoS0 publications.

surface_catalog.name: PINGREQ
surface_catalog.summary: Client liveness probe handled by the broker after CONNECT.

surface_catalog.name: PINGRESP
surface_catalog.summary: Broker response to PINGREQ with zero remaining length.

surface_catalog.name: DISCONNECT
surface_catalog.summary: Client requests connection termination; broker closes the associated connection.

message_or_command_entries.name: fixed_header
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: byte1 packet_type_and_flags followed by MQTT Remaining Length varint of 1 to 4 bytes
message_or_command_entries.summary: The first byte selects packet type and flags; Remaining Length gives the byte count of variable header plus payload.

fields.name: packet_type
fields.summary: High nibble of the first byte maps to mqtt_packet_type_t values.

fields.name: remaining_length
fields.summary: Variable-length integer parsed byte by byte with continuation bit and a maximum encoded length of four bytes.

message_or_command_entries.name: CONNECT
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: protocol_name string, protocol_level byte, connect_flags byte, keep_alive u16, client_id string
message_or_command_entries.summary: The example decoder accepts protocol name MQTT and level 4, records clean_session, keep_alive, and client_id, and ignores unsupported optional payloads.

fields.name: protocol_name
fields.summary: Length-prefixed string that must equal MQTT.

fields.name: protocol_level
fields.summary: Single byte that must equal 4 for MQTT 3.1.1.

fields.name: clean_session
fields.summary: Derived from connect_flags bit 1 and stored on the session.

fields.name: keep_alive
fields.summary: Unsigned 16-bit value parsed from CONNECT and stored on the session; active timeout enforcement is not implemented.

fields.name: client_id
fields.summary: Length-prefixed string parsed from the CONNECT payload and stored on the session.

message_or_command_entries.name: SUBSCRIBE
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: packet_id u16 followed by repeated topic_filter string and requested_qos byte
message_or_command_entries.summary: The decoder requires fixed header flags 0x02 and parses all topic filter/QoS pairs into a subscribe payload.

fields.name: topic_filter
fields.summary: Length-prefixed string stored in the router subscription table.

fields.name: requested_qos
fields.summary: Low two bits of the requested QoS byte are parsed; broker grants QoS0 for every accepted filter.

message_or_command_entries.name: PUBLISH
message_or_command_entries.syntax_or_layout: topic_name string, optional packet_id for QoS greater than 0, remaining bytes as payload
message_or_command_entries.summary: PUBLISH decoding captures DUP, QoS, RETAIN, topic name, optional packet id, and opaque payload; broker processing only routes QoS0.

fields.name: topic_name
fields.summary: Length-prefixed topic name used as the dispatch key for subscription matching.

fields.name: qos
fields.summary: QoS bits are decoded from the fixed header; values above 0 are ignored by broker handling.

fields.name: retain
fields.summary: Retain flag is decoded and preserved when forwarding QoS0, but retained-message storage is not implemented.

fields.name: payload
fields.summary: All bytes after the variable header are treated as opaque application payload.

field_constraints.condition: CONNECT protocol_name is not MQTT or protocol_level is not 4
field_constraints.required_action: decoder rejects the packet and broker handler is not invoked
broker does not route or acknowledge the publication in this minimal implementation

state_nodes.name: accepted_connection
state_nodes.summary: A TCP connection has been accepted and a session object exists, but CONNECT may not have completed.

state_nodes.name: connected_session
state_nodes.summary: CONNECT has been processed and the session has client_id, clean_session, and keep_alive fields set.

state_nodes.name: subscribed_session
state_nodes.summary: Connected session has one or more topic filters recorded in the router/topic tree.

state_nodes.name: closed_connection
state_nodes.summary: Connection file descriptor has been closed and router/session-manager cleanup removes associated subscriptions and session state.

transitions.summary: Broker marks session connected and sends CONNACK accepted.
Broker stores each topic filter and sends SUBACK return code 0x00 for each filter.
Broker routes the publication to matching subscribers without changing publisher session state.
Broker sends PINGRESP and keeps the session connected.

transitions.trigger: SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, or PINGREQ before CONNECT
transitions.summary: Broker closes the connection if these packets arrive before the session is connected.
Broker closes the connection and removes subscriptions and session records during close handling.

timers_and_constants.name: keep_alive
timers_and_constants.value_or_rule: Parsed from CONNECT and stored, but not actively enforced by this example broker.

invariants.summary: Application packets that require an established MQTT session should close the connection when received before CONNECT.
Session identity in routing tables is the connection file descriptor used as session id.

dispatch_keys.name: packet_type
dispatch_keys.summary: Broker dispatches decoded packets by mqtt_packet_type_t in a central switch.

dispatch_keys.name: topic_name
dispatch_keys.summary: QoS0 PUBLISH routing uses the topic name to find matching subscriber session ids.

dispatch_keys.name: topic_filter
dispatch_keys.summary: SUBSCRIBE registers topic filters that may include + or # wildcards.

dispatch_targets.name: broker_packet_handler
dispatch_targets.summary: Central broker handler implements CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, PINGREQ, and DISCONNECT behavior.

dispatch_targets.name: message_router
dispatch_targets.summary: Router owns subscription updates and publish fanout to matching sessions.

dispatch_targets.name: topic_tree
dispatch_targets.summary: Topic tree stores filter-to-session associations and performs wildcard matching.

matching_rules.summary: The + wildcard matches exactly one topic level.
The # wildcard matches only when it occupies the last filter level.
When several filters match the same session, fanout de-duplicates session ids before forwarding.

resource_objects.name: mqtt_connection
resource_objects.summary: Owns a socket fd, input buffer, output queue, peer string, and closed flag.

resource_objects.name: mqtt_session
resource_objects.summary: Wraps a connection and stores connected flag, client_id, clean_session, and keep_alive.

resource_objects.name: subscription
resource_objects.summary: Associates a topic filter with one or more session ids inside the topic tree.

resource_objects.name: publish_payload
resource_objects.summary: Represents a decoded PUBLISH topic, payload bytes, QoS, retain, dup, and optional packet id fields.

lifecycle_rules.summary: A session is created when a TCP connection is accepted and added to the session manager.
A session is marked connected only after a valid CONNECT packet is handled.
Subscriptions are removed when the connection closes and the session is removed from the session manager.
Decoded packet-owned strings and payload buffers are freed after packet callback processing.

persistence_scope.name: in_memory_only
persistence_scope.summary: The example broker has no retained-message persistence, offline session persistence, or durable subscription store.

error_matrix.condition: Malformed or unsupported CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE, or PUBLISH body encountered by decoder
error_matrix.required_action: decoder returns false for the packet; current broker read path does not explicitly close for every decode failure

error_matrix.condition: SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, or PINGREQ received before CONNECT

error_matrix.required_action: ignore the publication in this minimal broker; QoS1/2 acknowledgements are intentionally deferred

defaults.name: suback_granted_qos
defaults.value_or_rule: 0x00 Granted QoS0 for each topic filter

recommended_values.name: validation_profile
recommended_values.value_or_rule: Use external MQTT clients with QoS0 for end-to-end validation.

hard_bounds.name: mqtt_string_length
hard_bounds.value_or_rule: Length-prefixed strings are represented by uint16_t and cannot exceed 65535 bytes in encoder paths.

hard_bounds.name: read_chunk
hard_bounds.value_or_rule: Connection reads use 16 KiB chunks and grow the input buffer dynamically.

configurable_bounds.name: listen_port
configurable_bounds.value_or_rule: Broker accepts an optional command-line port; README documents default 1884.

security.name: authentication
security.summary: Username/password authentication and authorization are not implemented in this example scope.

security.name: tls
security.summary: TLS transport is outside the current example broker scope; transport is plain TCP.

must_support_surface.name: CONNECT
must_support_surface.summary: Accept valid MQTT 3.1.1 CONNECT and reply with CONNACK accepted.

must_support_surface.name: CONNACK
must_support_surface.summary: Encode CONNACK with return code 0x00 for accepted connections.

must_support_surface.name: SUBSCRIBE
must_support_surface.summary: Accept connected-client SUBSCRIBE packets and register filters.

must_support_surface.name: SUBACK
must_support_surface.summary: Reply to SUBSCRIBE with one Granted QoS0 return code per filter.

must_support_surface.name: PUBLISH
must_support_surface.summary: Route QoS0 PUBLISH messages to matching subscribers and encode forwarded QoS0 PUBLISH packets.

must_support_surface.name: PINGRESP
must_support_surface.summary: Encode and send PINGRESP for PINGREQ.

must_support_state_behaviors.name: session_after_connect
must_support_state_behaviors.summary: Track connected status, client_id, clean_session, and keep_alive per connection after CONNECT.

must_support_state_behaviors.name: subscription_lifecycle
must_support_state_behaviors.summary: Maintain in-memory subscriptions and remove all subscriptions for a session on close.

must_support_state_behaviors.name: incremental_stream_decode
must_support_state_behaviors.summary: Decode complete packets from a connection buffer and leave incomplete packet bytes for later reads.

must_support_error_paths.name: pre_connect_application_packet
must_support_error_paths.summary: Close on SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, or PINGREQ before CONNECT.

must_support_error_paths.name: unsupported_qos_publish
must_support_error_paths.summary: Do not implement QoS1 or QoS2 flows in the minimal scope.

must_support_limits.name: remaining_length_varint
must_support_limits.summary: Support MQTT Remaining Length varint decoding and encoding.

must_support_limits.name: topic_filter_wildcards
must_support_limits.summary: Support + and terminal # topic filter wildcards.

may_defer_features.name: QoS1_QoS2
may_defer_features.summary: PUBACK, PUBREC, PUBREL, PUBCOMP, retransmission, and exactly-once state are outside this example scope.

may_defer_features.name: authentication
may_defer_features.summary: Username/password authentication and authorization are not implemented.

may_defer_features.name: will_messages
may_defer_features.summary: Will message parsing, storage, and publication are not implemented.

may_defer_features.name: retained_and_offline_persistence
may_defer_features.summary: Retained messages, offline session persistence, and durable storage are not implemented.

may_defer_features.name: unsubscribe
may_defer_features.summary: UNSUBSCRIBE/UNSUBACK are not part of the README supported packet list even though router internals expose unsubscribe helpers.

implementation_assumptions.name: server_only_target
implementation_assumptions.summary: The downstream target should generate broker/server code; publishers and subscribers are external clients used for validation.

implementation_assumptions.name: qos0_only
implementation_assumptions.summary: The minimum runnable broker accepts and forwards QoS0 messages only.

implementation_assumptions.name: in_memory_runtime
implementation_assumptions.summary: Session and subscription state are in memory and tied to live TCP connections.

planning_inputs.protocol_summary: Minimal MQTT 3.1.1 broker subset implemented in C over TCP + epoll. The planning target is a broker that accepts external clients, handles CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE, QoS0 PUBLISH routing, PINGREQ, and DISCONNECT, and intentionally defers full MQTT features.
planning_checklist: 报文模型与编解码范围
required_codec_scope: MQTT fixed header and Remaining Length varint
implementation_axes: TCP event loop and connection buffers
critical_stateful_behaviors: Session is created at accept and marked connected only after CONNECT.
Subscriptions are associated with session ids and removed on connection close.
Incomplete byte-stream packets remain buffered until complete.
error_handling_obligations: Close when application-level packets arrive before CONNECT.
Treat QoS1/2 as out of scope for minimum planning.
Record decoder-failure close policy as an implementation risk because current example code does not close for every decode failure.
persistence_and_lifecycle_obligations: Clean router and session-manager records when a connection closes.
implementation_risks: Decoder silently skips unsupported packet types when decode_one returns false in mqtt_decoder_feed.
CONNECT optional fields are not parsed, so clients using username, password, or Will may not interoperate with the minimal broker.
Requested SUBSCRIBE QoS values are masked to low two bits and always granted as QoS0.
consistency_findings: README scope, packet enum, broker handlers, and encoder/decoder coverage agree on the minimum packet surface.
Router exposes unsubscribe helpers, but the protocol packet surface does not include UNSUBSCRIBE in the minimal README scope.

open_questions.question: Should the planning agent preserve the current decoder behavior that ignores unsupported or malformed decoded packets, or should the generated spec require closing the connection on all decode failures?
open_questions.suggested_followup: Decide whether this debug facts file should mirror the example exactly or use MQTT-compliant close-on-protocol-error behavior for generated specs.

open_questions.question: Should keep_alive remain a stored-but-unenforced field in minimum_v1, or should planning add an active timeout timer?
open_questions.suggested_followup: For parity with the example project, keep it stored-only; for stronger MQTT behavior, add timer requirements.

open_questions.question: Should CONNECT optional fields such as Will, username, and password be rejected explicitly or ignored in this debugging scope?
open_questions.suggested_followup: If interoperability testing uses common MQTT clients with credentials disabled, leave these optional fields deferred.

evidence_index.excerpt: MQTT 3.1.1 subset broker implemented with TCP + epoll; target is broker server only, with external clients used for validation.
Supported subset lists CONNECT to CONNACK, SUBSCRIBE QoS0 to SUBACK, QoS0 PUBLISH forwarding, PINGREQ to PINGRESP, and DISCONNECT.
The README maps modules to network, protocol codec, broker, session, topic tree, and message router responsibilities.
The broker executable runs as ./mqtt_broker [port], defaults to port 1884, and is validated with mosquitto clients using QoS0.
Current limits state QoS1/2, authentication, Will, retained message persistence, and offline session persistence are not implemented.
mqtt_packet_type_t defines CONNECT, CONNACK, PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE, SUBACK, PINGREQ, PINGRESP, and DISCONNECT plus payload structs.
mqtt_decoder_feed parses fixed header byte, Remaining Length varint, waits for complete packets, invokes a callback, frees packet data, and reports consumed bytes.
CONNECT decoding requires protocol string MQTT, protocol level 4, parses connect flags, keep_alive, and client_id.
SUBSCRIBE decoding requires fixed header flags 0x02, reads packet_id, then repeated filter strings and QoS bytes.
PUBLISH decoding reads topic name, dup, qos, retain, optional packet_id for QoS greater than zero, and remaining payload bytes.
Encoder functions build CONNACK, SUBACK, and PINGRESP packets using fixed headers and Remaining Length encoding.
mqtt_encode_publish_qos0 builds a PUBLISH fixed header, Remaining Length, topic string, and payload, with optional retain flag.
On accept, the broker creates a session for the connection and adds it to the session manager.
handle_packet processes CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, PINGREQ, DISCONNECT, sends responses, routes QoS0 publish, and closes pre-CONNECT application packets.
on_data feeds the connection input buffer to mqtt_decoder_feed and consumes decoded bytes after callback processing.
On close, the broker removes the session from the router and session manager.
Session state stores connection pointer, connected flag, client_id, clean_session, keep_alive, and derives session id from connection fd.
The router subscribes session ids to filters, removes sessions, matches subscribers for a publish topic, and sends encoded QoS0 PUBLISH packets.

evidence_index.section_hint: Topic filter storage and wildcard match
evidence_index.excerpt: The topic tree stores filter entries, supports + as one-level wildcard, # only at the last level, and returns unique matching session ids.
The TCP server creates the listening socket, accepts clients, and dispatches epoll read/write/close events through callbacks.
Connection objects hold input bytes, support consuming decoded bytes, queue outbound chunks, flush with send, and close the socket.
